 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 11-01-2022 at about 11.00 to 11.30 a.m., the petitioner was crossing the road near HQTC Gate, Bellari road, Bengaluru, for delivering the item to the customer, with all care and cautiously, by observing the vehicles plying on the road.
At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477, came from Mekhri Circle, in rash and negligent manner, with high speed and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Ramaiah Memorial Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident, he was working as food delivery boy and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Sadashivanagar Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further it is contended that, the insured/owner does not have proper and valid fitness certificate to use the vehicle on the road.
Further it is contended that, the alleged accident was not due to either rash or negligent up keep of the alleged vehicle in question.

On the contrary, petitioner who was proceeding on the road without observing the traffic, without care and cautious, not abiding the traffic rules and regulations and Jai Kumar.S vs Arbaz Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28330957/
2

sentences.text: failed to take required expected standard of care and precaution while using public place.
Hence he was sole responsible for the alleged accident.

The petitioner who is said to be the pedestrian and crossing the road, seems to have contributed to the cause of the alleged accident to a greater extent and was guilty of higher degree of contributory negligence.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of offending motorcycle and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 11-01-2022 at about 11.00 to 11.30 a.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle, bearing Reg.
No. KA-01-JM- 8477 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 23 documents as Ex.P.1 to 23.
Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely Agilasithan and Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as P.W.2 and P.W.3 and closed his side.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its representative/Assistant Manager as R.W.1 and got marked seven documents as Ex.R.1 to 7.
7.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 11-01-2022 at about 11.00 to 11.30 a.m.,
when the petitioner was crossing the road near HQTC Gate, Bellari road, Bengaluru, for delivering Jai Kumar.S vs Arbaz Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28330957/
3 the item to the customer, with all care and cautiously, by observing the vehicles plying on the road,
the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477, came from Mekhri Circle, in rash and negligent manner, with high speed and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as food delivery boy and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 23 documents as Ex

. Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R. with first information statement, Ex.P.2 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.5 is true copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.6 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report, Ex.P.7 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 is notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioner,
Ex.P.10 is notarized copy of driving licence, Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of registration certificate,
Ex.P.12 is discharge summary, Ex.P.13 are medical bills (total 4), Ex.P.14 are prescriptions (total 6),

Ex.P.15 is statement of accounts, Ex.P.16 are x-rays (total 5), Ex.P.17 are medical bills (total 20),
Ex.P.18 is authorization letter, Ex.P.19 is copy of police intimation, Ex.P.20 is copy of MLC extract,
Ex.P.21 are in-patient case sheets (total 2), Ex.P.22 is clinical report and Ex.P.23 is recent x-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was crossing the road near HQTC Gate, Bellari road, Bengaluru.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injury to his left leg.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477 and dashing the same to the petitioner.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-JM-8477 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place not due to rash or negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477 as alleged by the petitioner, but the same has occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner, who was crossing the road without observing the movement of vehicles on the road, without taking care and caution and without following the Jai Kumar.S vs Arbaz Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28330957/
4 traffic rules and regulations.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner who is said to be the pedestrian and crossing the road, seems to have contributed to the cause of the alleged accident to the greater extent and was guilty of higher degree of contributory negligence.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative/Assistant Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to sole negligence of the petitioner or he has contributed to the cause of accident to a greater extent.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-JM-8477 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was crossing the road near HQTC Gate, Bellari road, Bengaluru and due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on the left leg.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to sole negligence of the petitioner himself and there was no negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestions made in his cross-examination that, the said accident has taken place due to self negligence and there was no fault on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-JM-8477.
13.

Further, the Ex.P.2 sketch and Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the middle of 30 feet wide Mekhri Circle- Hebbal road, opposite to HQTC Gate,
Bellary road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was crossing the said road.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to the negligence of petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM- 8477.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the rider of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-JM-8477 and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident 14

. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.12 discharge summary, Ex.P.16 x- rays (total 5), Ex.P.21 inpatient case-sheets (total 2), Ex.P.22 clinical report Jai Kumar.S vs Arbaz Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28330957/
5 and Ex.P.23 x-ray
it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has suffered head injury with left leg proximal tibia and fibula bones type III B compound fracture.
The same is deposed by P.W.3, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. No doubt, as rightly argued by the learned counsel for respondent No.2, there is delay of 06 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the petitioner/complainant in the Ex.P.1 first information statement has stated the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint.

He has clearly stated that, after taking treatment and undergoing surgery at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
thereafter discussing with his relatives and deciding to lodge the complaint, he has lodged the complaint late.
Further, it is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.text: Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."
16. There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above reason for delay stated in the Ex.P.1 FIR and first information statement of the complainant.

In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly provided by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

17. Further, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that, the medical records,
particularly the contents of MLC Register extract and Discharge summary, clearly goes to show that,
petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional Police and the respondent No.1 has lodged a false concocted complaint and falsely implicated the insured motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477 in the alleged accident.

In Ex.P.20 MLC Register extract, it is clearly mentioned as follows, " H/o RTA, patient is a pillion rider, hit by another 2 wheeler, at around 11:00 A.M., on 11- 01-2022, near Mekri Circle, Bellary Road, Bengaluru.
The same is mentioned in Ex.P.21 Discharge summary also.

But, firstly it is pertinent to note that, the history of accident noted in the MLC register is not stated by the petitioner or his family members, but, the same is stated by one Nitin, said to be the friend of petitioner.
The P.W.1 has unequivocally stated in his cross-examination that, the said Nitin is unknown to him.
Secondly, there is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the said Nitin is the friend of petitioner and he was the eye-witness to the said accident.

In such circumstances, in absence of cogent and corroborative evidence, mere on the basis Jai Kumar.S vs Arbaz Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28330957/
6 of entry made in the MLC register, on the say or information provided by some unknown person to the injured, it cannot be held that, the petitioner in collusion with the Police and the respondent No.1 has lodged a false concocted complaint, by suppressing the true facts and circumstances of the accident.
Even, nothing with respect to same has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the respondent No.2 has not made any efforts to prove the contents of said documents i.e. Ex.P.20 & 21, by examining the author of said documents or examining the alleged friend of the petitioner by name Nitin.

Therefore, in such circumstances,
there is no other option before this Court, except to hold that, the above contentions taken by the respondent No.2 are false.

18. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, taken place on 11-01-2022 at about 11.00 to 11.30 a.m., opposite HQTC Gate, Bellary road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM- 8477.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JM-8477 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained head injury with left leg proximal tibia and fibula bones type III B compound fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.

To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of Jai Kumar.S vs Arbaz Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28330957/
7 his Aadhar card and driving licence, which are marked as Ex.P.9 and 10.
As per Ex.P.9 and 10, the date of birth of the petitioner is 25-12-1994.
The accident has taken place on 11-01-2022 at about 11:00 to 11:30 a.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is considered as 27 years.

Further, the P.W.3,
who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered head injury with left leg proximal tibia and fibula bones type III B compound fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 40% physical disability of left lower limb and 13%
physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.12 discharge summary, Ex.P.16 x-rays (total 5), Ex.P.21 inpatient case sheets (total 2), Ex.P.22 clinical report and Ex.P.23 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions that,
there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 11-01-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 01-01-2024, which is after lapse of two years from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been some reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fractures to the petitioner are united, with implants in situ.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as food delivery boy and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was working as food delivery boy and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

Therefore,

8 in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 27 years is 17.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 8/100 X 17 = Rs.2,52,960/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 24 medical bills, as per Ex.P.13 and 17.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.2,700/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,700/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. head injury with left leg proximal tibia and fibula bones type III B compound fracture.
As per Ex.P.12 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 6 days from 26-01-2022 to 31-01-2022, in Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further, as per P.W.3, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.

In such circumstances,
certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.12 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 6 days in Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.1000 x 6 = Rs.6,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.12 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 6 days from 26-01-2022 to 31-01-2022, in Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru.

vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Chikkamaranahalli, Devasandra, MSRIT,
Bengaluru, the accident has taken place opposite HQTC Gate, Bellary road, Bengaluru and the petitioner has taken treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru.

vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 6 days as in-patient at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.

Therefore, Rs.15,500 x 2 = Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 27 years and unfortunately he has suffered head injury with left leg proximal tibia and fibula bones type III B compound fracture.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

22. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:

sentences.text: Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

To establish the same the petitioner has produced the certified copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.5.

As per the said document, the rider of offending vehicle by name Yaseen A., was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA- 0120200032207 to ride the said vehicle, as on the date of accident and the said vehicle was insured by respondent No.2 insurance company, vide Policy No.67030231210800001519, valid from 13-08-2021 to 12- 08-2022.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA- 01-JM-8477 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,90,460/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,90,460/- (Rupees three lakh ninety thousand four hundred and sixty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
